## design

Build and check software from a brief and a check command, on its own branch in a git worktree: of the repository `target` names, or of a new project. Once its reviews pass it opens a pull request (a new project's private GitHub repository is created then), unless noPr. No reusable mode is required. Prefer wf_open default_pack/design with user gates.

Documentation: [refactory/docs/cli.md](../../../refactory/docs/cli.md)

## graph-control

Preview or queue boundary pause/resume/stop/rerun/redeliver/acknowledge/amend-command/withdraw/confirm-completion/skip controls. Recovery preserves saved routes and rejects unknown side effects or stale fingerprints; a rerun of a failed run takes acknowledge_failure once its side effects are inspected. resume --acknowledge-failure also starts an owner for a failed checkpoint. acknowledge transitions an executing or failed checkpoint whose owner died. amend-command corrects a run's setup, check or generate command. withdraw removes a stale queued control. stop on a terminal run signals the lingering owner directly. redeliver brings a finished or failed-at-deliver run up to date with main in one command. confirm-completion writes a person-only completion_override into spine-status.json, allowing update_goal complete despite a non-done status. skip queues a person's skip for a check node (a runtime_evidence producer); the source 'person' is hard-coded.

Documentation: [refactory/docs/live-control.md](../../../refactory/docs/live-control.md)

```json
{
  "description": "preview or queue a graph boundary control",
  "doc": "refactory/docs/live-control.md",
  "examples": [
    {
      "arguments": {
        "action": "preview",
        "node": "emit",
        "run": "/tmp/example-run"
      },
      "explanation": "Preview or queue boundary pause/resume/stop/rerun controls. Recovery preserves saved routes and rejects unknown side effects or stale fingerprints; a rerun of a failed run takes acknowledge_failure once its side effects are inspected."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "action": "acknowledge",
        "run": "/tmp/example-run"
      },
      "explanation": "Acknowledge an executing, failed or paused checkpoint whose owner died: moves pending delivery markers and mismatched outputs to set-aside, writes an SHA-bound acknowledgement so recovery accepts the checkpoint."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "action": "amend-command",
        "check": "pnpm test && python -m pytest -q tests",
        "note": "added pytest to the check",
        "run": "/tmp/example-run"
      },
      "explanation": "Correct a run's check (or --setup / --generate) command: records the change in facts.json command_history, queues a rerun control with commandCorrection semantics so the spine accepts a due node."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "action": "withdraw",
        "node": "control-id-to-remove",
        "run": "/tmp/example-run"
      },
      "explanation": "Remove a queued control that was never applied, so it does not affect the next owner. Refuses if the control has already been applied."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "action": "redeliver",
        "run": "/tmp/example-run"
      },
      "explanation": "Bring a finished or failed-at-deliver run's pull request up to date with main: merges current main, regenerates, re-checks and pushes, starting the owner process. Equivalent to rerun --node deliver plus resume, without needing --text, --revision or a preview."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "action": "confirm-completion",
        "run": "/tmp/example-run"
      },
      "explanation": "Write a person-only completion_override into spine-status.json, allowing update_goal complete despite a non-done status. The override is bound to the current status and invocation; it is cleared when recordStatus() writes a different status."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "action": "skip",
        "node": "check",
        "run": "/tmp/example-run"
      },
      "explanation": "Queue a person's skip for a check node (a runtime_evidence producer). The source 'person' is hard-coded. After queuing, resume the run with `refactory graph-control resume --run <dir> [--acknowledge-failure]`."
    }
  ],
  "interfaces": {
    "chat": "Unavailable as a direct chat mutation; use the documented CLI/panel route.",
    "cli": "python -m refactory_dsh.console graph-control",
    "panel": "Graph boundary controls and recovery preview."
  },
  "parameters": {
    "acknowledge_failure": {
      "default": false,
      "description": "confirm that side effects of the failed node have been inspected; required for rerun of a failed run",
      "flags": [
        "--acknowledge-failure"
      ],
      "nargs": 0,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "action": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "",
      "enum": [
        "pause",
        "resume",
        "stop",
        "preview",
        "rerun",
        "acknowledge",
        "amend-command",
        "withdraw",
        "redeliver",
        "confirm-completion",
        "skip"
      ],
      "flags": [],
      "nargs": null,
      "position": 0,
      "positional": true,
      "required": true,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "check": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "new check command (amend-command)",
      "flags": [
        "--check"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "generate": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "new generate command (amend-command)",
      "flags": [
        "--generate"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "node": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "",
      "flags": [
        "--node"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "note": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "why the command was changed (amend-command)",
      "flags": [
        "--note"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "project": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "repository root (default: found)",
      "flags": [
        "--project"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "revision": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "",
      "flags": [
        "--revision"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "run": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "a run directory or run id",
      "flags": [
        "--run"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "runs_root": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "the directory runs live under, one subdirectory per run; this is not the loop's --runs-root, which is the run directory itself",
      "flags": [
        "--runs-root"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "setup": {
      "default": "",

Recovery preserves saved routes and rejects unknown side effects or stale fingerprints; a rerun of a failed run takes acknowledge_failure once its side effects are inspected. resume --acknowledge-failure also starts an owner for a failed checkpoint. acknowledge transitions an executing or failed checkpoint whose owner died. amend-command corrects a run's setup, check or generate command. withdraw removes a stale queued control. stop on a terminal run signals the lingering owner directly. redeliver brings a finished or failed-at-deliver run up to date with main in one command. confirm-completion writes a person-only completion_override into spine-status.json, allowing update_goal complete despite a non-done status. skip queues a person's skip for a check node (a runtime_evidence producer); the source 'person' is hard-coded.",

## cli:ceo

Run a named mode or author a package/artifact from a brief in the terminal; worker file defaults apply at preparation. CEO conversation and graph worker routes are distinct.

Documentation: [refactory/docs/cli.md](../../../refactory/docs/cli.md)

```json
{
  "description": "describe what you want: the CEO designs or builds it (or run the mode you name)",
  "doc": "refactory/docs/cli.md",
  "examples": [
    {
      "arguments": {
        "knob": [
          "step=1",
          "target=5"
        ],
        "what": "counting_pack/fixed_step"
      },
      "explanation": "Run a named mode or author a package/artifact from a brief in the terminal; worker file defaults apply at preparation. CEO conversation and graph worker routes are distinct."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "check": "python -m pytest -q",
        "mode": "design",
        "target": "/path/to/repository",
        "what": "add a --json flag to the report command"
      },
      "explanation": "Change an existing repository: the run works on its own branch in a worktree of it, and the checkout at /path/to/repository is left as it is. Once its reviews pass it opens a pull request into the repository's default branch, which its approval gate names first (a run approved up front with --approve says it when it starts); --no-pr keeps the branch local. Without --target, a design run starts a new project in ~/refactory-projects, whose private GitHub repository is created at delivery."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "check": "python -m pytest -q",
        "mode": "design",
        "refine": "https://github.com/owner/repository/pull/12",
        "review_comments": true,
        "what": "rename the --json flag to --format json, as the review asked"
      },
      "explanation": "Follow up an open pull request: a new run starts from its branch, designs straight from the pull request (its description and diff; no research or strategy step, unless --refine-design full), goes through the full review, and pushes onto that branch, fast-forward only, leaving its title and description alone."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "check": "python -m pytest -q",
        "mode": "design_fast",
        "target": "/path/to/repository",
        "what": "add a --json flag to the report command"
      },
      "explanation": "The same change with one strategist, coder and focused QA agent: it works in a worktree of the repository on its own branch, as design does, but has no approval gate, so it opens no pull request and takes no --no-pr, --refine or --review-comments; its work stays on the run's branch, which its report names."
    }
  ],
  "interfaces": {
    "chat": "Unavailable as a direct chat mutation; use the documented CLI/panel route.",
    "cli": "refactory ceo",
    "panel": "Unavailable as a dedicated panel control; use the documented CLI or chat route."
  },
  "parameters": {
    "base": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "design and design_fast: the commit, branch or tag to start from",

## cli:doctor

Inspect prerequisites, the run model and the chosen provider's configured credential (never the headless profile's default) without a model call; with --run, also report a run's driver pin state. Configured does not mean authenticated.

Documentation: [refactory/docs/cli.md](../../../refactory/docs/cli.md)

```json
{
  "description": "check local prerequisites and sandbox credential configuration (no model request)",
  "doc": "refactory/docs/cli.md",
  "examples": [
    {
      "arguments": {},
      "explanation": "Inspect prerequisites, the run model (--provider/--model, else the stored choice, else what the first run would choose) and that provider's configured credential without a model call; configured does not mean authenticated."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "run": "/path/to/run"
      },
      "explanation": "Check a specific run's driver pin state: its recorded commit, profile name, and whether a pin exists."
    }
  ],
  "interfaces": {
    "chat": "Unavailable as a direct chat mutation; use the documented CLI/panel route.",
    "cli": "refactory doctor [--run DIR]",
    "panel": "Unavailable as a dedicated panel control; use the documented CLI or chat route."
  },
  "parameters": {
    "model": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "model to check (default: the stored model choice)",
      "flags": [
        "--model"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "provider": {
      "default": "",
      "description": "provider route to check (default: the stored model choice)",
      "flags": [
        "--provider"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    },
    "run": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "check a specific run's driver pin state",
      "flags": [
        "--run"
      ],
      "nargs": null,
      "positional": false,
      "required": false,
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "purpose": "Inspect prerequisites, the run model and the chosen provider's configured credential (never the headless profile's default) without a model call; with --run, also report a run's driver pin state. Configured does not mean authenticated.",
  "reviewed_schema": "70ed865990a4b3979383d83aa6cae6fa005f787dea18cc94e4f389a5e317e469"
}

## cli:model

The one model choice every run uses (the refactory profile's agent-default-model, shared with Settings → Models). A run with no choice and no flag is refused, or on a first run uses the only provider with a key. set stores it; show reads it.

Documentation: [refactory/docs/models.md](../../../refactory/docs/models.md)

```json
{
  "description": "the model every run uses: one choice, shared with Settings \u2192 Models",
  "doc": "refactory/docs/models.md",
  "examples": [
    {
      "arguments": {
        "model_action": "set"
      },
      "explanation": "Store the model every run uses, where Settings \u2192 Models keeps it: `refactory model set --provider deepseek-official --model deepseek-v4-pro`. Only that entry of the profile patch changes. --provider/--model on a command override it for that run."
    },
    {
      "arguments": {
        "model_action": "show"
      },
      "explanation": "Show the stored model choice and the file it is stored in, as JSON; exits 1 when none is chosen."
    }
  ],
  "interfaces": {
    "chat": "Unavailable as a direct chat mutation; use the documented CLI route.",
    "cli": "refactory model {set --provider <p> --model <m>, show}",
    "panel": "Unavailable as a dedicated panel control; use Settings \u2192 Models."
  },
  "parameters": {
    "model_action": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "",
      "enum": [
        "set",
        "show"
      ],
      "flags": [],
      "nargs": "A...",
      "position": 0,
      "positional": true,
      "required": true,
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "purpose": "The one model choice every run uses (the refactory profile's agent-default-model, shared with Settings \u2192 Models). A run with no choice and no flag is refused, or on a first run uses the only provider with a key. set stores it; show reads it.",
  "reviewed_schema": "f10bd7347dd90563346c2b4b9790d80ae0d3988d70a9426d093f2e3ef8d27fd9"
}
```

## annealing_pack/anneal

hill-climb a greedy circle packing by accepting non-worsening moves. Inspect declared ports and Task inputs before launch. Optimize only when scored; higher is better.

```json

  "description": "hill-climb a greedy circle packing by accepting non-worsening moves",
  "edges": [

      "source": "iterations_gate",
      "target": "perturb_circle"

      "condition": null,
      "source": "perturb_circle",
      "target": "accept_or_revert"

    {
      "condition": null,
      "source": "seed_placement",

## circle_packing/adaptive

population search over circle placements with a budget gate. Inspect declared ports and Task inputs before launch. Optimize only when scored; higher is better.

```json
{
  "description": "population search over circle placements with a budget gate",
  "edges": [
    {
      "condition": null,
      "source": "accept",
      "target": "select_parent"
    },
    {
      "condition": "reloop",
      "source": "budget_check",

    },
    {
      "condition": "proceed",
      "source": "budget_check",
      "target": "exit"
    },
    {
      "condition": null,
      "source": "eval",
      "target": "accept"
    },
    {
      "condition": null,
      "source": "generate",
      "target": "budget_check"
    },
    {
      "condition": null,
      "source": "seed_run",
      "target": "select_parent"
    },
    {
      "condition": null,
      "source": "select_parent",
      "target": "generate"
    },
    {
      "condition": null,
      "source": "task_input",
      "target": "seed_run"
    }
  ],
  "gates": [
    {
      "id": "budget_check",
      "user": false
    }
  ],
  "guidance": "This pipeline's generator is deterministic, so raising `budget` alone re-evaluates the same candidate. The score moves on `order` and `grid`, and on adding a step that varies the sample -- the `restart_on_stall` block. `acceptance_mode` and `selector` move it little.",
  "id": "circle_packing/adaptive",
  "nodes": [
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.circle_packing.ops:accept_or_reject",
      "id": "accept",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [
        "acceptance_mode"
      ],
      "notes": "keep the candidate when it beats its parent",
      "role": "ceo"
    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.circle_packing.ops:budget_check",
      "gate_kind": "fn",
      "id": "budget_check",
      "kind": "gate",
      "knobs": [],
      "notes": "reloop while budget remains",
      "role": "ceo"
    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.circle_packing.ops:evaluate_candidate",
      "id": "eval",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [],
      "notes": "score the candidate with the task's rule",
      "role": "ceo"
    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.circle_packing.ops:finish",
      "id": "exit",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [],
      "notes": "publish the number the outer loop maximizes",
      "role": "ceo"
    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.circle_packing.ops:generate",
      "id": "generate",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [
        "grid",
        "order",
        "seed"
      ],
      "notes": "draw the next candidate from the resolved generator settings",

    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.circle_packing.ops:seed_run",
      "id": "seed_run",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [],
      "notes": "seed the population with the task's own baseline heuristic",
      "role": "ceo"
    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.circle_packing.ops:select_parent",
      "id": "select_parent",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [
        "selector",
        "seed"
      ],
      "notes": "choose the individual the next candidate comes from",
      "role": "ceo"
    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.circle_packing.ops:task_input",
      "id": "task_input",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [

## counting_pack/fixed_step

count up to a target in fixed steps; no RNG, so no seed knob. Inspect declared ports and Task inputs before launch. Optimize only when scored; higher is better.

```json
{
  "description": "count up to a target in fixed steps; no RNG, so no seed knob",
  "edges": [
    {
      "condition": "proceed",
      "source": "check",
      "target": "finish"
    },
    {
      "condition": "retry",
      "source": "check",
      "target": "step"
    },
    {
      "condition": null,
      "source": "start",
      "target": "step"
    },
    {
      "condition": null,
      "source": "step",
      "target": "check"
    }
  ],
  "gates": [
    {
      "id": "check",
      "user": false
    }
  ],
  "guidance": "`step` is the lever: the count overshoots the target whenever `step` does not divide it, so moving `step` moves `closeness` directly. `step = 1` always lands exactly on the target. This mode has no RNG, so there is no seed knob.",
  "id": "counting_pack/fixed_step",
  "nodes": [
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.counting_pack.ops:check",
      "gate_kind": "fn",
      "id": "check",
      "kind": "gate",
      "knobs": [],
      "notes": "retry while the count is below the target, then proceed to the result",
      "role": "ceo"
    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.counting_pack.ops:finish",
      "id": "finish",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [],
      "notes": "publish the count the run reached, the number of steps it took, and closeness = 1 / (1 + abs(final_count - target))",
      "role": "ceo"
    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.counting_pack.ops:start",
      "id": "start",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [
        "target"
      ],
      "notes": "open the count at zero, record the target the gate stops at, and begin the empty trace; the same op serves both modes",
      "role": "ceo"
    },
    {
      "call": "refactory_packages.counting_pack.ops:step_fixed",
      "id": "step",
      "kind": "op",
      "knobs": [
        "step"
      ],
      "notes": "add one increment at this step index and append it to the trace",
      "role": "ceo"
    }
  ],
  "parameters": {
    "step": {
      "default": 2,
      "description": "the step size: the largest increment one random_walk step may add, and the exact increment every fixed_step step adds",
      "frozen": false,
      "kind": "int",
      "range": [
        1,
        4
      ],
      "value": 2,
      "values": []
    },
    "target": {
      "default": 5,
      "description": "the count the loop stops at; the gate proceeds once the count reaches it",
      "frozen": false,
      "kind": "int",
      "range": [
        1,
        9
      ],
      "value": 5,
      "values": []
    }
  },
  "ports": [],
  "scored": true,
  "usage": {
    "doc": "refactory/docs/getting-started.md",

## default_pack/design

Build a software artifact from a brief, name and acceptance command, as commits on the run's own branch in a git worktree: of the repository `target` names, or of a new project when it names none. Research, strategy and the design go straight to the approval gate, with no design reviewer: the design is written once to a light template (Summary, Changes, Tests), a claims check lists what it cannot confirm, and only a design with no ## Changes goes back for a rewrite (`design_review_attempts`, default 1); everything else is shown on the approval card. A scoped change (a refine, or one whose research footprint is small) skips the perspectives step, and a refine by default (`refine_design=light`) skips research and pitfalls too: its design starts from the pull request's description and diff. The builder works in a prepared clone of the last attempt (installs, setup and generate done), where it changes the code and runs the tests its change touches and the brief's own example (the first self-check runs the whole check); the clone's diff becomes the attempt. Before the reviews start, an attempt's first self-check runs the whole check once beside an early asks judge, which reads the diff against the brief's asks and the approved corrections; the attempt's own failures and anything the judge finds not built go back to the builder as one fix-up without spending an attempt (`self_check_fixups` times an attempt; past that, failures stop the attempt and not-built items alone go on to the reviews, listed for the QA judge and Overwatch), a fix-up's self-check runs the last failures and what the fix-up changed within `self_check_timeout_s`, and a failure the base shares is inherited unless the brief or a correction names it. The command runs in that worktree beside the separate QA reviews (on the commit both see, reusing the first self-check's run while the attempt is unchanged) and stays binding; a QA judge then reads the reviews and decides whether the build goes on or back, and Overwatch judges acceptance with an audit of the person's gate corrections as evidence (a correction given after the approval is applied to the design before the builder's next round, because every send-back to the builder goes through the corrections step, and Overwatch does not pass the change while one is unapplied); final current validation evidence is required. Only an ask, a correction, a failed health check or a critical or high defect sends the build back, and a correction Overwatch finds unmet always does; other findings are listed on the pull request as follow-ups. A judge whose verdict cannot be read is asked again once (`judge_rereads`), with no builder round. Once they pass, the branch is delivered as a pull request (into the branch its base came from, or the default branch), which the approval gate's question names first (`pr=0` keeps it local, with its pull request text in pull-request.md and finishing commands in delivery.json; `refine` updates an open one, rewriting only the sections delivery wrote in its description). When a limit stops the build (the check's, the reviews', all attempts', or refused emissions') at an applied commit with current check evidence, that commit is delivered as a draft pull request listing what is unresolved, marked [check failing] when its check fails.

    "purpose": "Build a software artifact from a brief, name and acceptance command, as commits on the run's own branch in a git worktree: of the repository `target` names, or of a new project when it names none. Research, strategy and the design go straight to the approval gate, with no design reviewer: the design is written once to a light template (Summary, Changes, Tests), a claims check lists what it cannot confirm, and only a design with no ## Changes goes back for a rewrite (`design_review_attempts`, default 1); everything else is shown on the approval card. A scoped change (a refine, or one whose research footprint is small) skips the perspectives step, and a refine by default (`refine_design=light`) skips research and pitfalls too: its design starts from the pull request's description and diff. The builder works in a prepared clone of the last attempt (installs, setup and generate done), where it changes the code and runs the tests its change touches and the brief's own example (the first self-check runs the whole check); the clone's diff becomes the attempt. Before the reviews start, an attempt's first self-check runs the whole check once beside an early asks judge, which reads the diff against the brief's asks and the approved corrections; the attempt's own failures and anything the judge finds not built go back to the builder as one fix-up without spending an attempt (`self_check_fixups` times an attempt; past that, failures stop the attempt and not-built items alone go on to the reviews, listed for the QA judge and Overwatch), a fix-up's self-check runs the last failures and what the fix-up changed within `self_check_timeout_s`, and a failure the base shares is inherited unless the brief or a correction names it. The command runs in that worktree beside the separate QA reviews (on the commit both see, reusing the first self-check's run while the attempt is unchanged) and stays binding; a QA judge then reads the reviews and decides whether the build goes on or back, and Overwatch judges acceptance with an audit of the person's gate corrections as evidence (a correction given after the approval is applied to the design before the builder's next round, because every send-back to the builder goes through the corrections step, and Overwatch does not pass the change while one is unapplied); final current validation evidence is required. Only an ask, a correction, a failed health check or a critical or high defect sends the build back, and a correction Overwatch finds unmet always does; other findings are listed on the pull request as follow-ups. A judge whose verdict cannot be read is asked again once (`judge_rereads`), with no builder round. Once they pass, the branch is delivered as a pull request (into the branch its base came from, or the default branch), which the approval gate's question names first (`pr=0` keeps it local, with its pull request text in pull-request.md and finishing commands in delivery.json; `refine` updates an open one, rewriting only the sections delivery wrote in its description). When a limit stops the build (the check's, the reviews', all attempts', or refused emissions') at an applied commit with current check evidence, that commit is delivered as a draft pull request listing what is unresolved, marked [check failing] when its check fails.",

## default_pack/design_fast

Build a small artifact with one sequential strategist, coder and QA agent, as commits on the run's own branch in a git worktree: of the repository `target` names, or of a new project when it names none (`worktree=0` writes .factory/artifacts instead; `source_project` copies a directory there). The check runs in that worktree before focused QA. It has no approval gate, so it opens no pull request: the branch is left for you to push. The coder works in a prepared clone of the last attempt, whose diff becomes the attempt.

## default_pack/edit

Revise an existing mode package and validate the revision before separate QA and Overwatch. Supply revision_of, name and brief. allow_regression=true skips original execution and numerical comparison, while revised execution and intent evidence remain mandatory.

```json

  "guidance": "The score is what Lean accepted, so no structural edit can raise it: only a proof the checker passes can. The retry gate rotates through the strategies, so `attempts` decides whether a run gets there at all and `strategy` decides whether it gets there on the first try, which is worth 0.1. `library` switches to the mathlib problem, which needs the `mathlib` tool and is where the default strategy fails.",
